page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.medium is a general-purpose instance powered by a single-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 ARM64 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 1 dedicated vCPU, 1 physical core, and 4.0 GB of system memory. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 59 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In benchmark testing, the single-core CPU performance via stress-ng registers at 1493.49, placing it in the average tier. However, due to its single-core limitation, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core fall into the lower performance percentiles. Memory bandwidth tests show read speeds of 59.37 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 19.34 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, while write bandwidth is measured at 9.33 GB/sec. Redis SET operations achieve 1.18 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 1.15 GB/sec.

The m6gd.medium offers a cost-effective entry point for ARM64 development and lightweight workloads that benefit from high-speed local NVMe storage. The primary tradeoff is the single-core constraint, which limits parallel processing capabilities and results in lower multi-threaded performance. The baseline network bandwidth is also limited to 0 Gbps, making it less suitable for network-intensive applications.

This instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, local development and testing of ARM64 applications, small-scale caching layers, and low-traffic web serving where local temporary storage is required.
